value.body: A vehicle validation engineer checks that a vehicle or component works as designed — for durability, performance, emissions, noise or safety. Employers include vehicle makers, component suppliers, testing agencies and engineering services firms. A typical day involves preparing test plans, fitting sensors, running tests on rigs or tracks, and analysing data.

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Data loggers, sensors, test rigs, MATLAB

items.label: Rules tested against
items.value: Central Motor Vehicles Rules and AIS standards
items.note: Type approval is done through notified testing agencies

items.label: UG students in Automobile Engineering
items.note: AISHE lists this separately from Mechanical Engineering (~4.2 lakh UG students). Counts only institutions that responded to AISHE, so national totals may be higher.

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers join vehicle makers, suppliers or testing agencies as graduate engineer trainees, often after an internship. Student vehicle projects (formula-style, off-road or electric car competitions) commonly come up in interviews.

value.title: At a glance
items: Work can involve travel to test tracks and field trials in different climates.
Electric-vehicle testing (batteries, motors) is a growing part of the work.
Next roles: test lead, homologation engineer, product engineer.
